executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across Europe and the Americas. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, elevated dengue and chikungunya transmission across the Americas region, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with residual Northern Hemisphere circulation. Additional signals include measles resurgence, pertussis increases, mpox activity, and yellow fever alerts, indicating a high-burden multi-pathogen environment requiring coordinated surveillance and response.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face simultaneous multi-pathogen threats in mid-2026, with H5N1, dengue, influenza co-circulation, and pertussis resurgence representing the highest-priority public health risks.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from ongoing animal reservoir circulation in the Americas
threats.action: Enhance human-animal interface surveillance, reinforce PPE protocols for exposed workers, accelerate prepandemic vaccine stockpiling, and activate One Health investigation teams

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated regional transmission
Historical pattern of hyperendemic multi-serotype circulation raising severe dengue and DHF risk
threats.action: Strengthen vector control and Aedes aegypti surveillance, activate early warning systems in high-incidence countries, and ensure clinical management capacity for severe dengue

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Onset)
signals: PAHO alert on 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Prior alert on simultaneous RSV and influenza co-circulation January 2026 indicating dual respiratory burden
threats.action: Activate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, increase ICU and antiviral stockpile readiness, and monitor for novel antigenic variants

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and resurging pertussis activity
Probable contribution of waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy to increased case counts
threats.action: Boost Tdap vaccination coverage especially in pregnant women and infants, investigate outbreak clusters, and review immunization program adherence

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing mpox transmission in the Americas
Risk of clade expansion and community spread in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Expand mpox vaccination to at-risk populations, strengthen contact tracing, and ensure laboratory diagnostic capacity across member states

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling measles cases in the Americas region
Ongoing immunization gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic creating susceptible cohorts
threats.action: Conduct supplemental immunization activities targeting under-vaccinated communities, intensify surveillance for rash-fever illness, and enforce travel-related vaccination requirements

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating yellow fever activity in the Americas
Epizootics in non-human primates historically precede human spillover events
threats.action: Reinforce yellow fever vaccination in endemic and at-risk zones, enhance epizootic surveillance in non-human primate populations, and review traveler vaccination requirements

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating chikungunya transmission
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika in Aedes-endemic zones amplifying arboviral burden
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya into arboviral surveillance platforms, reinforce vector control, and ensure clinical differentiation from dengue for accurate case management

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multi-pathogen ECDC weekly reports)

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis circulation in the context of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis campaigns raises concern for macrolide resistance emergence
Sustained bacterial co-infections during influenza seasons increase selective pressure for antimicrobial resistance in respiratory pathogens
No direct AMR pathogen-specific reports identified in source titles; indirect AMR risk elevated given multi-pathogen co-circulation and broad antibiotic use
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen co-circulation in the Americas (dengue, chikungunya, measles, mpox, influenza, pertussis) suggests compounding healthcare system strain
Persistent H5N1 activity in animal reservoirs across the Americas from November 2025 through March 2026 indicates endemic establishment rather than sporadic incursion
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in late April 2026 overlapping with residual Northern Hemisphere activity suggests year-round respiratory virus burden
Post-pandemic immunization gaps are driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis across the Americas
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports in April-May 2026 signals sustained elevated multi-threat environment in Europe
